transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

If you can hear the dryer running but the drum stays still, the most likely cause is the drive belt having snapped or slipped off. Less commonly, the motor may only be humming because its start capacitor has failed, or the drum supports may be binding. 1. Switch it off, unplug it, and empty the drum. Turn the drum slowly by hand. If it spins very freely with little resistance, that points to the belt being off or broken. If it is stiff, rough, grinding or stuck, a drum support/bearing or an item jammed around the drum is more likely. 2. Think about the load when it failed: a very heavy single item such as a duvet or rug can overload the drive. Do not keep running it with the drum stationary, as it can strain the motor. Tell me how the drum feels by hand: normal, very free, or stiff.
ok i turned it by hand with it unplugged and it spins really easy almost no resistance. normal load in it when it went, heard a twang then a thud and a bit of a rubber smell at the time

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. This points to the drive belt having snapped or come off. A drum that turns almost freely, with the dryer otherwise running, plus the twang, thud and rubber smell, is the classic pattern. The tension/idler pulley may also have failed and thrown the belt off. Do not use the dryer again. The rubber smell means the drive has been slipping or damaged, and it needs a qualified engineer to inspect the belt path, tension pulley and motor area before it is run. The repair is commonly a belt, sometimes with the jockey/idler tension pulley if that is worn or seized. The drum supports/bearing are unlikely because the drum is not stiff or rough by hand. A motor capacitor is also less likely because the noise and smell at the moment it failed fit a belt-drive failure much better.

candidates: Drive belt has come off or snapped (high)
Motor start capacitor or motor fault (medium)
